title.narrative: DEPLOYMENT OF YOUTH ELECTION DAY OBSERVERS

description.narrative: 1. Sampling of Polling Stations and Deployment of Youth Observers For the Coalition to strategically cover a segment of polling stations to make a meaningful assessment of the electoral process, 3401 polling stations were sampled from the 276 constituencies using the official polling station data obtained from the Electoral Commission. The trained youth observers were deployed to 1000 of the sampled non-PVT polling stations across the country. Their observation activities were supervised by Regional Coordinators and Constituency Supervisors. The observers, using the developed standardised checklist, reported on various aspects of the polling process, including the start of polls, voting, close of polls, counting, and declaration of results at polling stations. The data from the reports were collated and analyzed at the CODEO National Information Center for public consumption. 2. DEVELOPMENT OF OBSERVATION MATERIALS CODEO used various observation materials to help in the regulation of the conduct of election day observers. These observation materials included training manuals, checklists, and incident forms. The purpose of these materials was to provide quick reference or information to observers on the field, whether roaming or stationed observers on their roles and responsibilities during the election period and to equip them with the requisite tools for successfully observing and communicating their observations with the Secretariat. These manuals provided an overview of CODEO’s 2024 domestic election observation project, the code of conduct for observers, the roles and responsibilities of observers, explanation, and instructions on completing the checklists and critical incident forms, schedule of activities and timelines, timelines for reporting and contact information of the Secretariat and Regional Coordinators. The Secretariat also developed a standardized checklist that comprehensively enabled observers to elicit information on all aspects of the polling process from the start of polls, voting, close of polls, counting, and declaration of results at polling stations. In addition, the critical incident form was developed. The critical incident form enabled observers to immediately report incidents that affected the smooth functioning of the electoral process anytime it occurred. The observation checklist and critical incident report forms were to guide observers on the correct texting format used for the submission of reports at the scheduled times. These materials were developed based on the global principles for the observation of elections and the various electoral laws, including the Constitutional Instrument (CI) 127. These forms included many different questions that informed the Secretariat on how the election was conducted by the officials of the electoral commission, party agents, security personnel, and voters, and whether electoral rules and regulations were followed.

policy-marker.narrative: The objective was to promote youth participation in election observation and contribute to the transparency and integrity of election processes. This initiative increased youth inclusion, participation, and representation in the electoral processes and also promoted public confidence in the elections and enhanced the integrity of the outcomes of the 2024 general elections.
